title: Wrong partner

brief.story: The greenhouse thermometer reads far too high. The sensor is a 10 kΩ thermistor (10 kΩ at 25 °C), and the voltage it makes with its fixed partner R1 should sit at mid-scale, about 4.5 V, at room temperature. It reads over 8 V.
brief.goal: Find the wrong part and fix it so the sensor voltage (column 8) is 4.3–4.7 V at 25 °C.

datasheet.title: RT1 · NTC thermistor
rows: R1 on top, RT1 to ground

hints: The sensor voltage is a divider: V = 9 V × RT1 ÷ (R1 + RT1). Measure it, then read R1’s bands.
For mid-scale (half of 9 V) the two halves of a divider must be equal.
R1 is 1 kΩ: 9 × 10 ÷ 11 = 8.2 V. Change it to 10 kΩ for 4.5 V.

spec.label: Sensor voltage
spec.explain: A sensor divider is most sensitive with its fixed resistor equal to the sensor’s middle value.

debrief: A resistive sensor (thermistor, light sensor, strain gauge) is read as one half of a divider. With the fixed half equal to the sensor’s value in the middle of its range, the output sits at half the supply and moves the most for each degree. A 1 kΩ partner squashed every reading up near 8 V, where a change in temperature barely shows.
